sourceBindings.text: A useful report says whose sample was tested, which values the learner measured, which values the trainer supplied, how each result was obtained, and what can actually be inferred. Practise with Field 3 and a separate tomato case; never turn model figures into your own observations.
Build a Field 3 report with identification, pH, texture, OM, P and K, clearly distinguishing learner measurements from trainer-supplied or demonstrated results and recording methods and units.
Interpret each value using a stated laboratory, crop and regional reference; identify gaps or missing methods instead of inventing a low/optimum/high class.
Give two justified, conditional tomato recommendations, prioritize one, and name the evidence required before an application rate or final field prescription.

sourceBindings.text: Discussion case: pH 5.5 and P 12 ppm
One minute think, two minutes pair, two minutes share. The example gives pH 5.5 and phosphorus 12 ppm; extraction method, crop and site are not given.
On the classroom chart alone, pH is below 6.0 and P below 15 ppm.
Record these as illustrative chart labels, not final fertilizer or lime advice.
Ask for the crop target, laboratory P method and recommendation, lime requirement and site conditions before a rate or field action.
A low example value raises a question; the supporting test and crop context determine the recommendation.

sourceBindings.text: Field 3 supplied model, separate from your sample
Model texture 45/35/20 loam and pH 6.4; trainer-supplied OM 2.1%, P 12 ppm and K 185 ppm.

Preserve the example's compost depth/incorporation and high-P product as source proposals; do not issue them as a dose without evidence.
A model illustrates report structure; it is not the learner's test result.

sourceBindings.text: Separate tomato written case: pH 5.4
A different farmer's tomato report states pH 5.4, OM 2.1%, P 12 ppm and K 185 ppm, without laboratory extraction methods or a location.
The classroom chart would call pH 5.4 low; OM 2.1% lies in its unclassified gap; P 12 and K 185 fall in its example low and optimum bands respectively.
Do not claim method-independent P/K categories or a measured crop nutrient deficit. Request the lab's method and local tomato guidance.

Two justified next actions could be: obtain a crop-specific lime requirement and site target before any lime rate; and seek a method-calibrated phosphorus and whole-nutrient plan before choosing a P source or rate. OM management can be assessed using material quality and field history.
Prioritize the action whose expected benefit and evidence are strongest for this field; state what could change that priority.
This pH 5.4 bank case is neither the pH 5.5 discussion example nor the pH 6.4 Field 3 model.

sourceBindings.text: soil test interpretation
A judgement about what a measured value means for a crop under a stated method and calibrated reference.
ppm
Parts per million as reported for an identified soil-test analyte and method; not by itself a fertilizer dose.
lime requirement
A laboratory or locally calibrated assessment used with crop target and soil conditions to estimate liming need; soil pH alone does not specify a rate.
extraction method
The laboratory procedure used to measure an index such as soil-test phosphorus; a result's interpretation depends on it.
organic matter
Soil material from living and formerly living sources; its reported percentage and interpretation depend on sampling and analytical method.
data provenance
A record of which value was personally measured, supplied, demonstrated, modelled or missing.
